chapter: Failure in St. Louis and the Omaha bands
title: Stranded in St. Louis and taken in by a family; dating it 1936
summary: Unable to hold the job and unrecommended, he stayed with a kind family; Dance works out the year as 1936.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: What happened to you, were you stranded or what happened?

Absolutely. Absolutely. I was stranded in every sense of the word. I went to St. Louis and I couldn't cut it, I couldn't play the music and I was so embarrassed, and naturally -- but I mean, what could you do. The guy couldn't use me. He recommended me to another band leader who was using a girl pianist because he didn't have a man who could play, and he would prefer to have a man but I couldn't read the music, I couldn't read that music good enough. I didn't have experience. And so there was nothing for me to do. They couldn't use me, you know. Unfortunate, it was just unfortunate, you know.

No, I wasn't frightened, no, because believe it or not I had made friends there, and I never will forget the family I stayed with. I stayed at their house like a relative. People were like that during those days, particularly if you were a musician or entertainer, you know, because they'd realize that you had this talent and they tried to help you because that was in their appreciation for your talent.
You haven't told me what year it was.
Wait a minute now, let's see. You
Well, no, let's just think. You were 17?
Well, I was 18. I would have to be 18.
No, that's all right, it's 1936, it's two 18's.
And we don't have to swear on the bible or anything but it's 1936.
Now, that shows you how much smarter you are than I am.
But that's what it is because that's interesting to know just what period that was.
Yes, well I'm glad you brought it up because like I said I'm very lax in facts like that.

Well, you see, people listening to you will want to relate it to what's happening in other places at that time, in those years. You know. So 1936. Well, then so what did you do? You stayed with these people, and what did you do?
